# Parikshan

> End-to-End (E2E) UI testing framework for Compose Multiplatform applications across Desktop (JVM), Web (Wasm), Android, and iOS. Write intent-based UI tests once in Kotlin, execute them across physical targets, and inspect unified HTML reports and video recordings.

---

## 1. Core Architecture & Mental Model

* **Intent-Based DSL**: Tests interact with UI elements using high-level user intents (`click`, `input`, `assertVisible`, `assertText`, `scrollUntilVisible`) rather than target-specific platform drivers.
* **Platform Isolation**: Tests reside in `src/commonTest/kotlin` as pure Kotlin Multiplatform code. Never import platform-specific packages (`java.io.*`, `java.lang.System`, `android.util.*`) in common test code.
* **Non-Invasive**: Production application code does not bundle testing frameworks, test harnesses, or mock drivers in production builds.

---

## 2. Selector Resolution Hierarchy

When an intent function accepts a `selector: String` (e.g., `click("login_button")`), the resolution engine matches in the following strict order:
1. **Explicit Compose Test Tag**: Matches `Modifier.testTag("tag")`.
2. **Exact Visible Text**: Matches the full visible text of buttons, labels, or input fields.
3. **Visible Substring / Content Description**: Matches partial visible text or accessibility content description (`Modifier.semantics { contentDescription = "..." }`).

For explicit matching, use typed selectors:
* `Selector.Tag("my_tag")`
* `Selector.Text("Exact Text")`
* `Selector.ContentDescription("Description")`

---

## 3. Test Authoring Patterns

### A. Standard Single-Actor Test
Used for typical single-user flows running across any target platform:

```kotlin
package sample.app

import io.github.aryapreetam.parikshan.e2eTest
import kotlin.test.Test

class LoginFlowTest {
  @Test
  fun testUserLogin() = e2eTest {
    input("username_input", "test_user")
    input("password_input", "secret123")
    click("login_button")
    assertVisible("Welcome back, test_user!")
  }
}
```

### B. Multi-Instance Testing (Same Target, Multiple Windows/Tabs)
Used when testing peer-to-peer interactions between multiple users on the same platform (spawns 2 Desktop windows or 2 isolated Web browser contexts):

```kotlin
@Test
fun testChatCollaboration() = e2eTest(listOf("alice", "bob")) { (alice, bob) ->
  alice.input("chat_input", "Hello Bob!")
  alice.click("send_button")

  bob.assertVisible("alice: Hello Bob!")
  bob.input("chat_input", "Hey Alice, received!")
  bob.click("send_button")

  alice.assertVisible("bob: Hey Alice, received!")
}
```

### C. Multi-Target Testing (Cross-Platform Actors)
Used when Alice runs on Desktop (JVM) while Bob runs on Web (Wasm) interacting across a shared backend:

```kotlin
@Test
fun testDesktopToWebCollaboration() = e2eTest(
  instances = mapOf("alice" to Target.Desktop, "bob" to Target.Wasm)
) { (alice, bob) ->
  alice.input("chat_input", "Message from Desktop")
  alice.click("send_button")

  bob.assertVisible("alice: Message from Desktop")
}
```

### D. Native File Picker Automation
Automates modal OS file dialogs and browser file upload inputs without blocking the UI thread:

```kotlin
@Test
fun testDocumentUpload() = e2eTest {
  withFilePicker("document.pdf") {
    click("upload_file_button")
  }
  assertVisible("document.pdf uploaded successfully")
}
```

---

## 4. Test Selection Decision Matrix

| Requirement | Recommended Declaration | Execution Command |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Single user flow / screen verification | `e2eTest { ... }` | `./gradlew e2eDesktopTest` (or `e2eWasmTest`, `e2eAndroidTest`, `e2eIosTest`) |
| Run single user flow on all targets | `e2eTest { ... }` | `./gradlew e2eTest --targets=desktop,wasm,android,ios` |
| Visual UI parity check across viewports | `e2eTest { ... }` | `./gradlew e2eTest --targets=jvm,wasm --sync` |
| Two users on Desktop or two tabs on Web | `e2eTest(listOf("alice", "bob")) { (alice, bob) -> ... }` | `./gradlew e2eDesktopTest` or `./gradlew e2eWasmTest` |
| One user on Desktop and one on Web | `e2eTest(instances = mapOf("alice" to Target.Desktop, "bob" to Target.Wasm))` | `./gradlew e2eTest --targets=jvm,wasm` |
| Native file upload / attachment | `withFilePicker("file.ext") { ... }` | Any target test task |

---

## 5. Gradle Command-Line Options

```bash
# Target Selection
--targets=desktop,wasm,android,ios   # Select physical targets to execute

# Layout & Sizing (Desktop & Web)
--layout=side-by-side                # Auto-tile Desktop and Web viewports side-by-side
--window-size=360x720                # Set viewport dimensions (Width x Height)
--desktop-window-position=X,Y        # Screen coordinates for primary Desktop window
--wasm-window-position=X,Y           # Screen coordinates for Web browser window
--app-mode                           # Launch Web browser without browser navigation chrome

# Execution Modes
--sync                               # Lockstep barrier synchronization across active targets
--watch                              # Re-run matching tests on source file save
--video                              # Capture MP4 video recordings of test runs
--step-delay=500                     # Delay in milliseconds between intent steps
```

---

## 6. Guardrails for AI Agents

1. **Deterministic Sequential Flows**: Multi-actor tests should execute sequentially (`alice.input(...) -> bob.assertVisible(...)`) unless testing true concurrency.
2. **Never Fabricate Targets**: Only use physical targets (`Target.Desktop`, `Target.Wasm`, `Target.Android`, `Target.Ios`).
3. **No Thread Sleep**: Use `waitFor("element_tag")` or built-in auto-waiting on `click` / `assertVisible` instead of `Thread.sleep` or `delay`.
4. **Scope Isolation**: Single-actor tests use `E2ETestScope`. Multi-actor tests receive `E2EMultiInstanceScope` with destructured `Actor` instances.
